problems.title: Transiting extra-solar planet.
problems.statement: The transit of an extra-solar planet (TrES-3b) across a star (TrES-3) was observed by the 1-m telescope of Weihai Observatory (WHO) on April 16, 2009, using the broad-band V filter and a PI CCD. The photometric data (selected part from the original one) are given in the Table 6 (see separate sheet), the time is in Julian days, and $m_{\mathrm{V}}$ is the V-band magnitude.

parts.statement: Plot the transit light curve (magnitude vs time), determine the moment of mid-transit (the deepest transit) and write result (in Julian days) in form of «$T_{\mathrm{mid}} = \ldots$», estimate the duration of the transit (in days) in form of «$T_{\mathrm{d}} = \ldots$», determine the depth of the transit (in magnitudes) in form of «$D = \ldots$» .

Give the formula and calculate the radius of the extra-solar planet TrES-3b $R_{\mathrm{p}}$ (in units of the radius of Jupiter: $R_{\mathrm{Jupiter}}$, write the answer in form of «$R_{\mathrm{p}} = \ldots$»). The radius of the star (TrES-3) is known to be 0.813 radius of the Sun, $R_{\mathrm{s}} = 0.813\,R_{\mathrm{sun}}$.

Estimate the approximate value of the angle $i$, in unit of degrees (°) between the axis of this planet’s orbiting and the line of sight of the observer. Write the answer in form of «$i \approx \ldots$».

The next mid-transit moment after the above transit event was: JD = 2454939.578. The mass of the star (TrES-3) is known to be 0.924 mass of the Sun, $M_{\mathrm{s}} = 0.924\,M_{\mathrm{sun}}$. Calculate the orbital period of TrES-3b (in units of days, in form of «$P = \ldots$»), and the semi-major axis of the orbit (in units of au, in form of «$a = \ldots$»).

problems.title: Extinction in terrestrial atmosphere.
problems.statement:
Extinction is a term used in astronomy to describe light attenuation due to its absorption and scattering.

A star ($\alpha = 22^{\mathrm{h}}02^{\mathrm{m}}40^{\mathrm{s}}$, $\delta = +42^{\circ}14'41''$) was observed at different zenith distances on October 26, 2017 (after its upper culmination at 11:34:20 UT), at the Weihai Observatory (WHO) of Shandong University. Astronomers use parameter $F(z)$, air mass, as an extinction characteristic, $F(z) \approx 1/\cos(z)$ if the zenith distance ($z$) is smaller than 60°. The atmospheric extinction equation can be written as: $m_{\mathrm{V}} = m_0 + K\cdot F(z)$, where $m_0$ is the magnitude of the star without atmospheric extinction, $K$ is the atmospheric extinction coefficient. Table 7 (see separate sheet) gives the observing times (UT, in units of hour) and the measured magnitudes ($m_{\mathrm{V}}$) of the star.

parts.statement:
Draw the table (similar to that you see below) in your answer book. Calculate zenith distances, $z$, in unit of degrees (°), for given observing times in 1$^{\mathrm{st}}$ column, and write the result into the 2$^{\mathrm{nd}}$ column. Calculate the air mass ($F(z)$) for different zenith distances, and write the result into the 3$^{\mathrm{rd}}$ column.

| UT_obs (hour) | $z$ (°) | $F(z)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12.49484 |  |  |
|  |  |  |
Plot the scatter diagram between magnitudes ($m_{\mathrm{V}}$) vs. air mass ($F(z)$). Draw a straight dashed line on the plot to indicate the linear relation between $m_{\mathrm{V}}$ vs. $F(z)$.

Estimate the atmospheric extinction coefficient ($K$) and the magnitude of this star without atmospheric extinction ($m_0$) with help of graphical method, and write results in forms of «$K = \ldots$», «$m_0 = \ldots$».
Determine the magnitude ($m_{\mathrm{Z}}$) of this star as if it was observed in zenith, and write result in form of «$m_{\mathrm{Z}} = \ldots$».

solution.incompleteReason: The workbook supplies the calculation table and scatter chart, but no straight dashed fit line or final values for K, m₀ and mZ (parts 7.2–7.4).
